'''David J. Lockwood''' is a [[Canadian]] physicist and researcher emeritus at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC). He is also an adjunct professor at the [[University of Windsor]] in [[Windsor, Ontario]], editor of the journal ''Solid State Communications'', editor of the Springer book series "Topics in Applied Physics",<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/series/560 |title=Topics in Applied Physics}}</ref> and secretary-treasurer of the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]]. Lockwood is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]], the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Electrochemical Society]], and the [[Institute of Physics]].

== Early life ==
Lockwood was inspired to pursue physics at an early age by his [[Christchurch Boys' High School]] teacher, Henry (Swanny) Dyer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cap.ca/sites/cap.ca/files/article/2902/pic-69-3-4-medals-awards-2013.pdf |title=Cap Triumf Vogt Medal for Contributions to Subatomic Physics |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> He subsequently completed a B.Sc. (1964), M.Sc. (1966)<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lockwood |first=D. J. |title=The action of a sound field on colloids |date=1964 |degree=Master of Science |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/8024 |url=http://hdl.handle.net/10092/8024}}</ref> and Ph.D. (1969)<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lockwood |first=D. J. |title=Solid state studies : Raman spectroscopy and the lattice vibrations of CdCl2 and CdBr2 |date=1969 |degree=PhD |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/13789 |url=http://hdl.handle.net/10092/13789}}</ref> in [[Physics]] at the [[University of Canterbury]] in [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]]. His doctoral work, under Professor Alister McLellan, focused on [[Raman scattering]] from insulators.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cap.ca/wyp/profiles/davidlockwoodphdlineage.pdf |title=David J. Lockwood's Ph.D. Supervisor Lineage |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018033023/https://www.cap.ca/wyp/profiles/davidLockwoodPhDLineage.pdf |archive-date=18 October 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Between 1970 and 1971, Lockwood undertook post-doctoral research at the [[University of Waterloo]] with Professor Donald Irish, where he investigated the [[vibrational spectroscopy]] of [[solvated cations]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Donald E Irish - Publications|url=http://academictree.org/chemistry/publications.php?pid=72638|website=Academic Tree|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref> He then spent six years as a research fellow at [[Edinburgh University]], looking at the dynamical properties of structural phase transitions and [[antiferromagnets]]. These studies culminated in a DSc degree in physics from Edinburgh University in 1978.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lockwood|first=David J.|date=1978|title=Light scattering spectroscopy: studies of electronic excitations and atomic vibrations in matter |publisher=University of Edinburgh |hdl=1842/12453 |type=DSc |url=https://www.era.lib.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/12453|language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
In 1978, Lockwood moved to Canada to work at the [[National Research Council (Canada)|National Research Council]] (NRC), where his continued work on magnetic materials led to the publication of what would become a seminal book in the field, ''Light Scattering in Magnetic Solids'', co-written with Michael Cottam.<ref>{{cite book|title=Light scattering in magnetic solids (Book, 1986) |publisher=WorldCat.org |date=1999-02-22 |oclc=13185400 }}</ref> He turned his attention to the optical properties of [[superlattices]], semiconductor heterostructures, and [[nanostructures]], publishing some 600 papers and 39 books, as well as registering six US patents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nanoandgiga.com/~lockwood |format=PDF |title=Dr. David Lockwood |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-date=3 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225018/http://nanoandgiga.com/~lockwood |url-status=dead }}</ref> Lockwood has edited numerous scientific volumes, notably the ''Nanostructure Science and Technology'' series, and served on the editorial boards of several journals, such as ''Low Temperature Physics'', ''Physica E'', and ''Physics in Canada''. He has organised international conferences and served on over 50 committees, including within [[NATO]] and [[IUPAP]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cap.ca/en/bio/dr-david-lockwood |title=Dr. David Lockwood &#124; Supporting Physics Research And Education In Canada |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402123742/http://www.cap.ca/en/bio/dr-david-lockwood |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2016, Lockwood retired from the NRC. In July 2016, he was invested with the title of NRC Researcher Emeritus.

== Honours ==
[[File:David J. Lockwood in 2012.jpg|thumb|2012 Symposium]]
Lockwood has garnered significant recognition for his work, including the Canadian Association of Physicists' (CAP) Brockhouse Medal<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cap.ca/awards/press/2005-Lockwood.html |title=Press Releases |publisher=Cap.ca |date=2005-06-07 |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304061951/http://www.cap.ca/awards/press/2005-Lockwood.html |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the Royal Society of Canada's Tory Medal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marketwire.com/press-release/Royal-Society-Canada-Salutes-Excellence-Humanities-Sciences-Award-Winners-2005-541794.htm |title=The Royal Society of Canada Salutes Excellence in Humanities and Sciences: Award Winners, 2005 |publisher=Marketwire.com |date= |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> each awarded in 2005.

In 2010 the Electrochemical Society granted him the Centennial Outstanding Achievement Award,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electrochem.org/dl/interface/fal/fal10/fal10_p019-036.pdf |title=Special Meeting Section |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> and in 2011 he received the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Canadian Semiconductor Science and Technology Conference "in recognition of over 40 years of outstanding contributions to the generation and dissemination of knowledge related to materials science as revealed by optical spectroscopy".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cap.ca/en/article/dr-david-lockwood-receives-2011-lifetime-achievement-award |title=Dr. David Lockwood receives 2011 Lifetime Achievement Award &#124; Supporting Physics Research and Education in Canada |publisher=Cap.ca |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402101432/http://www.cap.ca/en/article/dr-david-lockwood-receives-2011-lifetime-achievement-award |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

A symposium in honour of David Lockwood was held at the 2012 Pacific Rim Meeting on Electrochemical and Solid State Science (PRIME 2012).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://electrochem.org/meetings/biannual/222/tp/reportTechProg_1202_D7.html |title=Technical Program |publisher=Electrochem.org |date= |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> In February 2013, Lockwood was granted the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal, which recognised significant achievements by Canadians in honour of the Queen's Jubilee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gg.ca/document.aspx?id=14019 |title=Diamond Jubilee Medal |publisher=Gg.ca |date= |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> Also in 2013, Lockwood was awarded the CAP Medal for Lifetime Achievement in Physics, the highest honour that a Canadian physicist can receive.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cap.ca/medal/publicity/press.php?year=2013&medal_id=5 |title=CAP Medal Press Release - 2013 Achievement |publisher=Cap.ca |date=2013-05-30 |accessdate=2015-03-27}}</ref> In February 2015, Lockwood was made a Fellow of the Institute of Physics of the UK.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://icanm2015.iaemm.com/Keynote-Lectures.php |title=Keynotes |publisher=Icanm2015.iaemm.com |date=2015-03-03 |accessdate=2015-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402183130/http://icanm2015.iaemm.com/Keynote-Lectures.php |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Lockwood was the 2019 recipient of the [[Gordon E. Moore Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Solid State Science and Technology]]. Lockwood was recognised for outstanding original contributions to the elucidation of the role of quantum-confinement effects in the optical and electrochemical properties of semiconductor nanostructures with applications in optoelectronics and photonics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.electrochem.org/moore-award |title=Gordon E. Moore Medal |publisher=electrochem.org }}</ref>

In 2022, Lockwood received an Honorable Mention in the IUPAP 100 Photo Contest under the category "At a Glance". In the photograph, Lockwood is seen aligning a laser beam from an argon ion laser for a Raman scattering experiment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iupap.org/centennial/satellite-events/iupap-100-photo-contest/ |title=IUPAP 100 |publisher=iupap.org |date= 27 June 2022|accessdate=2022-07-22}}</ref> The photo was also displayed outside UNESCO headquarters in Paris, and on the cover of the UNESCO publication commemorating the International Year of Basic Sciences.

In recognition of his extensive publication record in materials science, Lockwood ranked 99th in Canada in Research.com's 2023 Ranking of Best Scientists in this field, based on a D-index (Discipline H-index) metric. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.com/scientists-rankings/materials-science/ |title=Best Materials Science Scientists |publisher=research.com |date= |accessdate=2023-04-24}}</ref>
